title: Two dated sky positions give a periapse limit for bound Kepler pairs and a conditional WASP-105 test
abstract: We prove a lower periapse limit from two sky positions and their dates for a bound Kepler pair. An escape-speed envelope applies across the full interval. Conserved projected angular momentum then gives the limit. The method accepts limits on mass, distance and angle errors. It needs no instantaneous velocity or fitted orbit. None of 30,000 generated Kepler pairs violates the limit. A naive finite-difference substitution fails in 892 cases. For the published rounded WASP-105 scenario, exact angles give stellar periapse lower limits of 16.46 AU or 45.72 AU. These use distances of 169 pc or 217 pc. A specified quadrupole model includes general relativity and a static planet tide. In that model, excitation of a planet on star B to eccentricity 0.5 needs periapse below 0.0831 or 0.0647 AU. The initial planet eccentricity approaches zero. The finite-interval angle caps are 0.1350 and 0.0715 degrees. The published scenario has a change of 1.9 degrees. Combined absolute angle-error limits below 1.765 or 1.829 degrees would exclude that excitation model. A continuous planet-structure interval changes these thresholds to 1.695 or 1.792 degrees. We supply no calibrated orientation error, new astrometry, transit confirmation or secure host exclusion. The final calculation uses published scalar scenarios. The proof, code, generated test pairs and figures reproduce locally without external raw data.

display.caption: A bound from two astrometric epochs compared with the periapse cap for excitation of a planet on WASP-105 B. The angle-error allowance is assumed. No calibrated new angle measurement is supplied.
Tests on 30,000 generated exact Kepler pairs. The finite-interval lower bound never exceeds the true periapse. A naive instantaneous substitution fails in 892 curved arcs.

Prior necessary quadrupole excitation and instantaneous sky-motion bounds. We supply a bound valid across a finite interval and explicit input-error tests.
